title: Numbers 1–10
summary: Count from 1 to 10, read Arabic digits and exchange phone numbers.
intro: Arabic numbers are written with the digits ٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩, and a number is read from left to right even inside right-to-left text: ١٠ is ten. Today you finish the alphabet: م ن ه و ي, plus hamza ء, tāʾ marbūṭa ة and alif maqṣūra ى.
objectives: Give and ask for a phone number
Read the last letters of the alphabet

realLife.title: Swapping numbers
realLife.story: After class the teacher gives homework on page seven. Daniel has a question, so he asks Layla for her phone number, and Sami invites everyone to study at his house tomorrow.

sentences.en: What is your phone number? (to a man)
My number is five seven three.

dialogue.title: Phone numbers and homework
dialogue.culture: In Egypt, the Levant and the Gulf most people use the digits ٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩. In North Africa (Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia) the digits 0123456789 are common, and they are Arabic in origin too.

lines.ar: يَا طُلَّاب، الْوَاجِب فِي الصَّفْحَة رَقْم سَبْعَة. شُكْرًا وَمَعَ السَّلَامَة!
lines.en: Students, the homework is on page number seven. Thank you, and goodbye!

lines.ar: يَا لَيْلَى، مَا رَقْمُ هَاتِفِكِ؟ عِنْدِي سُؤَال عَنِ الْوَاجِب.
lines.en: Layla, what is your phone number? I have a question about the homework.

lines.ar: طَبْعًا! رَقْمِي: صِفْر، سَبْعَة، وَاحِد، اِثْنَان، أَرْبَعَة…
lines.en: Of course! My number is zero, seven, one, two, four…

lines.ar: مَهْلًا، مَهْلًا! بِبُطْء مِنْ فَضْلِكِ. صِفْر، سَبْعَة، وَاحِد…
lines.en: Wait, wait! Slowly, please. Zero, seven, one…

lines.ar: صِفْر، سَبْعَة، وَاحِد، اِثْنَان، أَرْبَعَة، ثَلَاثَة، تِسْعَة، ثَمَانِيَة.
lines.en: Zero, seven, one, two, four, three, nine, eight.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا! وَهٰذَا رَقْمِي: خَمْسَة، سِتَّة، عَشَرَة… لَا، صِفْر!
lines.en: Thanks! And this is my number: five, six, ten… no, zero!

lines.ar: الْأَرْقَام صَعْبَة قَلِيلًا فِي الْبِدَايَة، لٰكِنْ لَا مُشْكِلَة.
lines.en: Numbers are a little hard at the beginning, but no problem.

lines.ar: عِنْدِي فِكْرَة! نَحْنُ ثَلَاثَة طُلَّاب، وَالْوَاجِب عَشَرَة أَسْئِلَة.
lines.en: I have an idea! We are three students, and the homework is ten questions.

lines.ar: فِكْرَة جَمِيلَة! نَدْرُس مَعًا فِي الْبَيْت؟
lines.en: A great idea! Shall we study together at home?

lines.ar: نَعَم! تَعَالَوْا إِلَى بَيْتِي غَدًا فِي السَّاعَة الْخَامِسَة.
lines.en: Yes! Come to my house tomorrow at five o'clock.

lines.ar: مُمْتَاز! أَيْنَ بَيْتُكَ يَا سَامِي؟ مَا رَقْمُ الْبَيْت؟
lines.en: Excellent! Where is your house, Sami? What is the house number?

lines.ar: بَيْتِي قَرِيب، فِي شَارِعِ النِّيل، رَقْم تِسْعَة.
lines.en: My house is close by, on Nile Street, number nine.

reading.title: Numbers in a notebook
reading.ar: رَقْمُ بَيْتِ سَامِي تِسْعَة. رَقْمُ هَاتِفِ لَيْلَى: صِفْر، سَبْعَة، وَاحِد… الْوَاجِب فِي الصَّفْحَة رَقْم سَبْعَة.
reading.en: Sami's house number is nine. Layla's phone number: zero, seven, one… The homework is on page number seven.

quiz.prompt: How do you write 7 in Arabic digits?
At what time do the friends meet at Sami's house?
Which letter is the th of 'think'?
What does ة at the end of a word usually show?

completion: You did it! You know all the letters of the Arabic alphabet and can count to ten. Take the week test to open Week 2.
